title: Node-variant smokebench: K8s + driver/CUDA/NCCL validation notes
content:
Summary:
These are working notes from a quick smokebench we ran to validate matrix compatibility across a mix of node variants (A100, A30, T4), multiple OS distros, and a range of Kubernetes/kubelet and NVIDIA stack versions. Goal: identify minimal safe upgrade paths and obvious incompatibilities for the on-prem Terraform modules and upgrade playbooks. This doc is intentionally rough — results, commands, and next steps first, followed by a terse compatibility matrix and Terraform module callouts.

Scope and constraints:
- Cluster mix: 3 node types (a100-40gb, a30-24gb, t4-16gb), single cluster with node pools labeled by gpu-profile.
- Distros tested: Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 8.8, Rocky Linux 8.6 (quick test only).
- K8s versions: 1.25.7 (prod baseline), 1.26.4, 1.27.2 (canary).
- CUDA stacks: 11.8, 12.1 (NVIDIA driver requirements differ).
- Drivers: NVIDIA 525.x, 535.x, 540.x (on nodes constrained by OS packages).
- NCCL: 2.14.x, 2.16.x.
- Tests were run as non-privileged daemonset + a simple multi-GPU MPI job to surface NCCL issues.
- Terraform modules: we used private-deployments/gpu-nodepool v0.9 with small overrides for taints/labels.

Quick observations (high level):
- Ubuntu 22.04 nodes are the most forgiving across drivers; RHEL 8.8 required kernel-headers pinning for 540.x driver installs.
- CUDA 12.1 + driver 540 caused NCCL 2.14-based images to show subtle rank initialization failures on A30 in 1.27; upgrading NCCL to 2.16 fixed the symptom.
- K8s 1.27 + driver 540 + CUDA 12.1 produced a kubelet eviction spike when pods used GPU memory aggressively — appears related to stale device plugin metrics (we saw node-exporter GPU metrics balloon).
- T4 nodes consistently handled driver 535 and CUDA 11.8; newer driver installs sometimes required a reboot to clear old kernel module references.

Commands and snippets used (copy/paste from lab):
- Node prep (Ubuntu 22.04):
  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)
  # install driver (example 535)
  sudo bash NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-535.54.run --silent
  sudo reboot

- Check plugin + device visibility in k8s:
  kubectl get nodes -L gpu-profile
  kubectl describe node gpu-a100-01 | grep -i nvidia -A3
  kubectl run -i --tty gpu-debug --rm --restart=Never --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-base-ubuntu22.04 -- nvidia-smi -L

- NCCL smoke job (MPI-ish):
  kubectl apply -f tests/nccl-minimal-job.yaml
  # watch for timeouts and rank errors in pod logs
  kubectl logs -f nccl-smoke-0 -c runner

Observed failures and error signatures:
- "NCCL WARN Call to cudaMalloc failed" on A30 nodes when CUDA image (12.1) used NCCL 2.14; memory allocation succeeded on host but CUDA library reported mismatch. Root cause: driver/NVML expectations not aligned with NCCL build.
- kubelet OOM/eviction events only when running sustained multi-gpu workloads on 1.27. Reproducible when device-plugin exported stale topology fields — caused scheduler/eviction thresholds to miscalculate.
- Driver install on RHEL required explicit kernel-devel matching; install script would silently continue but modules failed to load without matching headers.

Compatibility matrix (summary lines, not exhaustive):
- K8s 1.25.x: OK with driver 525/535 + CUDA 11.8 for T4/A100. NCCL 2.14 recommended.
- K8s 1.26.x: OK with driver 535 + CUDA 11.8/12.1 on Ubuntu; RHEL needs extra packaging steps. NCCL 2.16 optional.
- K8s 1.27.x: Works with driver 535/540 + CUDA 12.1 but requires NCCL 2.16 and kubelet/device-plugin updates (see notes). Watch node-exporter metrics.
- Driver 540: preferred for CUDA 12.1 on A30; requires kernel header pinning on RHEL/rocky.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Keep driver bootstraping out of core node pool module; provide a separate "gpu-bootstrap" module that runs as a remote-exec or image-based DaemonSet to avoid long terraform runs when kernel headers mismatch.
- Module variables to add: expected_nvidia_driver (string), required_cuda (string), distro_kernel_headers (bool), auto_reboot_after_driver_install (bool).
- Example call (pseudo):
  module "gpu-nodepool-a30" {
    source = ".../private-deployments/gpu-nodepool"
    gpu_type = "a30"
    node_image = var.node_image_ubuntu_22_04
    expected_nvidia_driver = "540.44"
    required_cuda = "12.1"
    taints = { gpu = "true:NoSchedule" }
  }
- Prefer using an init-system container that validates kernel headers and writes a status file into hostPath (/var/lib/redwood/gpu-driver-ready) — Terraform can poll via local-exec to gate further resource creation (quick mitigation for drift).

Actionable upgrade guidance (short):
- For clusters on Ubuntu 22.04: prefer in-place upgrades to CUDA 12.1 + driver 535 first on a canary nodepool with NCCL 2.16 images. If stable for 48 hours under typical workloads, proceed to broader rollout.
- For RHEL/Rocky: stage a packaging job that builds driver kernel module RPMs for the exact kernel versions in the fleet; provide these RPMs as an artifact in the private repo. Avoid running .run installers in automated terraform flows.
- K8s 1.27: enable device-plugin v1.0.1+ builds and increase kubelet evictionWatermark pod thresholds temporarily during the rollout window.

Open questions / unknowns we should validate next:
- Does driver 540 + kubelet 1.27 consistently produce the GPU-metrics spike on other hardware vendors or is this A30-specific? We need wider sample.
- Can we automate NCCL version bumping in model-serving images without breaking legacy users? Build matrix and run nightly regression.
- Should the Terraform module include a validated-image catalog (node_image + expected_gpu_stack) to reduce ad-hoc combinations? Pros/cons: safer but more catalog maint.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- (Liam) Build a small RPM pipeline for 540.x driver for RHEL/Rocky; post artifacts to internal repo (due 2026-03-10).
- (Maya) Run 72h canary on Ubuntu 22.04 a30 pool with driver 535 + CUDA 12.1 + NCCL 2.16 images; collect node-exporter and kubelet metrics (due 2026-03-08).
- (Priya) Draft Terraform change for gpu-bootstrap module with gating file approach; prototype local-exec polling (due 2026-03-05).

Notes and links:
- Related playbook: confluence:/private-deploys/driver-upgrades (working draft)
- Slack thread: #private-deploys 2026-02-20 (discussion on 1.27 regressions)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912 (gpu-nodepool refactor)

Rough end-state recommendation (working):
- Adopt a two-track upgrade: (1) image-driven canaries (validated node_image + gpu_stack in catalog), (2) packaging-driven upgrades for RHEL families. Keep driver installs idempotent and observable via hostPath status files.

If anything above looks off, call out experiments to rerun. This doc will be iterated into a more formal playbook once canary data lands.

-- Ethan
